INFOBLOX_VIEW.description: Operator-supplied Infoblox view name forwarded into the ?view= query parameter on GET /wapi/v2.12/record:host (Infoblox DNS view — the namespace scope for split-DNS / multi-tenancy named under Data Management -> DNS -> Zones in the Grid Manager) and into the ?network_view= query parameter on GET /wapi/v2.12/network (Infoblox network view — Infoblox separates DNS views and network views; the IPAM surface doesn't carry a DNS view field, the closest analogue is the network view). Optional; empty / blank is interpreted as 'no view narrowing' and the dispatcher walks every host record / network the credentials can read. Whitespace is trimmed and URL-encoded server-side.

INFOBLOX_NETWORK_FILTER.description: Operator-supplied Infoblox network CIDR forwarded into the ?network= query parameter on GET /wapi/v2.12/network (exact CIDR match — WAPI supports the ~= and := modifier suffixes for regex / contains matches but exact match is the safest default for an operator-supplied playbook argument). Optional; empty / blank is interpreted as 'no CIDR narrowing'. NOT forwarded into the record:host surface (host records don't filter by network CIDR — they filter by name / IP / view). Whitespace is trimmed and URL-encoded server-side.

name: infoblox_ddi
title: Infoblox DDI (NIOS)
description: Infoblox DDI (NIOS) importer. Pulls DNS host records and IPAM subnet records from an Infoblox NIOS Grid Master via the WAPI REST surface and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON. Infoblox NIOS is the enterprise DDI (DNS, DHCP, IPAM) appliance suite — the Grid Master is the authoritative source-of-truth for DNS namespace, DHCP scope configuration and the IPAM tree of network containers, networks and IP-address objects — so this executor is the network-management cross-reference feed Faraday operators correlate the EDR / EASM / vuln-scanner agents' findings against to confirm whether a vulnerable IP is a known Infoblox-tracked host record on a managed subnet (and therefore in-scope for the network team) or an unmanaged stray on someone else's range. Each Infoblox record:host becomes one Faraday host (DNS host records ARE network-keyed since each host record carries an ipv4addrs / ipv6addrs projection anchoring the record to one or more tracked IP endpoints; the executor lifts the first ipv4addrs[].ipv4addr (or ipv6addrs[].ipv6addr as fallback) onto host.ip when present, falls back to the 0.0.0.0 sentinel for placeholder host records that don't carry an assigned address; the name / aliases projection lands on host.hostnames; the first ipv4addrs[].mac value lands on host.mac when present; view / network_view / comment / extattrs enrichment lands on host.description; the host record itself becomes one Faraday vulnerability with the [NETWORK] engine prefix). Each Infoblox network becomes one Faraday host on the 0.0.0.0 sentinel (IPAM network containers describe a subnet range, not a single IP endpoint; the CIDR lives in host.hostnames and host.description; the network record itself becomes one Faraday vulnerability with the [NETWORK] engine prefix). Endpoints used: GET {INFOBLOX_HOST}/wapi/v2.12/record:host?_paging=1&_max_results=N&_return_as_object=1[&view=<INFOBLOX_VIEW>] (canonical Infoblox DNS host-record inventory; returns the WAPI paging envelope {result, next_page_id} walked page-by-page via the opaque next_page_id cursor — next request sends ?_page_id=<id> — until the cursor is absent or the env-only INFOBLOX_PAGES cap is reached, default 5, clamped to [1, 50]; each record carries _ref, name, view (the DNS view this record lives in), ipv4addrs (list of nested {ipv4addr, configure_for_dhcp, mac} objects), ipv6addrs, aliases, comment, network_view, zone, extattrs; when INFOBLOX_VIEW is set the dispatcher forwards it as ?view=<name> so the walk only returns host records living in that DNS view), GET {INFOBLOX_HOST}/wapi/v2.12/network?_paging=1&_max_results=N&_return_as_object=1[&network_view=<INFOBLOX_VIEW>][&network=<INFOBLOX_NETWORK_FILTER>] (canonical Infoblox IPAM network-container inventory; same WAPI paging envelope; each record carries _ref, network (the CIDR a.b.c.d/PFX), network_view (Infoblox separates DNS views and network views — DNS views govern name resolution, network views govern address-space partitioning), comment, extattrs, members (the grid members handing out DHCP on this range), options, ipv4addr_count, utilization; when INFOBLOX_VIEW is set the dispatcher forwards it as ?network_view=<name> since the network surface doesn't carry a DNS view field; when INFOBLOX_NETWORK_FILTER is set the dispatcher forwards it as ?network=<value> exact CIDR match). Pagination is opaque-cursor via WAPI's next_page_id response field; the first request carries ?_paging=1&_max_results=100&_return_as_object=1; each subsequent request carries the same _paging / _return_as_object toggles plus ?_page_id=<cursor> (WAPI binds the operator filter to the cursor server-side so re-sending it rejects with 400). _max_results is fixed at 100 (a conservative default; WAPI accepts up to 1000). Auth: Infoblox NIOS WAPI uses HTTP Basic Auth. Operators provision a service account in the Grid Manager under Administration -> Administrators -> Admins with the API permission group attached (read-only is sufficient). The dispatcher carries credentials on every request as Authorization: Basic <base64(user:pass)>. INFOBLOX_HOST is the operator's Grid Master host (e.g. infoblox.mycorp.com); https:// is added automatically when the operator pasted in a bare FQDN. TLS verification is left to requests defaults (operators with self-signed appliance certs should set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE in the dispatcher env). Severity for host records / networks is always info (they're DDI inventory entries, not findings — the value is the cross-reference signal, not a vulnerability score). Tags: [infoblox_ddi, network, ddi, ipam, host-record|network].
